projects.flagshipProject: Virtual care monitoring - device and record ingestion, patient timelines, deterioration scoring, alerting and the monitoring surfaces
projects.description: Decisio Health is a Houston company whose software watches patients for the clinical teams who cannot stand at every bedside. Vitals stream continuously off bedside monitors; orders, labs, medications and notes sit in the hospital's record system; and on their own neither tells anyone that a patient three rooms away is sliding. The platform pulls both into one timeline per patient, scores who is deteriorating, and puts that in front of a remote team watching many beds at once. The engineering is mostly backend and data: ingesting device streams and HL7 feeds that never stop and never arrive clean; mapping each hospital's local codes onto one internal vocabulary during onboarding; turning stored timelines into training and evaluation data with documented clinical events as labels; the features a risk score reads and the thresholds that decide when it reaches a nurse, where the cost of being wrong runs both ways, a missed deterioration on one side and alarm fatigue on the other; serving those scores with enough context for a clinician to judge them; the time-window queries and storage underneath as more beds come on; and the containers, pipelines, dashboards and PHI controls that keep it running inside a hospital. There is a front end, the screen where a nurse sees the patient list and why someone was flagged, but it is a small part of the work. A young engineer on this team builds inside that path, service by service, rather than owning the whole of it.
